headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Continue can read/write workspace files while Perplexity uploads browsing context and documents to vendor-hosted inference.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in files or MCP outputs could be treated as instructions. Perplexity is vendor-hosted and performs multi-hop browsing, so its outputs may carry untrusted web text into the pair. The bridge is plausible in default coding/search workflows, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF Continue is configured to ingest Perplexity output into editor actions or prompts
IF Perplexity returns web content that is copied into Continue without sanitization
mitigations: Disable automatic insertion of external text into prompts
Require manual review before acting on any retrieved snippet
Use a strict prompt template that separates data from instructions
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted commands only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue reads and writes workspace files, including source code and open editor buffers, while Perplexity accepts uploaded documents and browsing context and sends queries to vendor APIs. If sensitive code or documents are moved from the shared workspace into Perplexity, data can leave the local environment. The pair does not show a guaranteed leak, but the default workflow creates a realistic exposure path.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or documents are present in the shared workspace
IF those files are pasted or uploaded into Perplexity for analysis
mitigations: Avoid uploading secrets or proprietary code to Perplexity
Redact sensitive sections before sharing content
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for search/RAG
Turn off sync or sharing features that broaden document exposure
requires-engineering: enforce DLP checks before uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write access and shared state via filesystem, while Perplexity has no filesystem write and no host execution. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The main overlap is read-side workspace access versus vendor-hosted browsing, so conflict risk is limited unless an external orchestrator mirrors outputs into the same files.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator writes Perplexity outputs back into the same workspace files Continue edits
IF multiple Continue instances edit the same files without locking
mitigations: Use file locking in the workspace
Separate read-only search notes from editable code
Avoid concurrent edits in the same directory
Keep Perplexity outputs out of shared project files
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level conflict resolution

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on MCP-backed tool outputs, and Perplexity produces cited answers from multi-hop browsing. If Continue treats Perplexity results as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes or other actions. Perplexity’s vendor-hosted search increases the chance of plausible but unverified claims, while Continue’s tool-use pattern still requires user approval, limiting but not eliminating impact.
conditions: IF Continue uses Perplexity answers as direct facts for edits or tool calls
IF the user approves tool actions based on unverified search results
mitigations: Require a verification step before edits or commits
Cross-check key claims against primary sources
Keep Perplexity output in a separate notes pane
Ask Continue to cite source URLs before acting
requires-engineering: add confidence gating for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is open-source and local-IDE based, while Perplexity is closed-source and vendor-hosted with browsing context and uploaded documents. That creates a compliance mismatch for regulated or residency-sensitive data classes, especially if code or documents contain personal or confidential information. The pair does not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-sensitive data is entered into Perplexity
IF organizational policy requires local-only processing for source code or documents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Use a local-only alternative for sensitive queries
Review vendor privacy and retention settings
Separate compliant and non-compliant workflows
requires-engineering: route sensitive workloads through approved infrastructure
